claims.text: High-temperature mechanical and thermoelastic behavior in refractory high-entropy alloys is governed by heterogeneous lattice distortions.
Localized heterogeneous lattice strain fields alter dislocation core structures.
Heterogeneous lattice strain causes multiple dislocation kinks and jogs and bidirectional cross-slip.
Lattice distortions favor enhanced edge-dislocation activity.
Edge dislocations can govern high-temperature strength and strength retention in BCC refractory high-entropy alloys.
Unusual dislocation behaviors caused by heterogeneous lattice strain underpin a strength–ductility synergy.
The distortion-induced change in dislocation dynamics produces a distinctive or modified thermoelastic response.
TiZrHfNbMo0.1 is an example of a fully homogenized, single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy suitable as the initial state.
Larger atomic-size mismatches increase lattice distortion.
Reducing atomic-size differences lowers lattice distortion.
At high temperature, the high-distortion alloy will have a higher frequency of dislocation kinks and jogs than the low-distortion control.
At high temperature, the high-distortion alloy will retain greater strength than the low-distortion control.
At high temperature, the high-distortion alloy will retain greater hardness than the low-distortion control.
At high temperature, the high-distortion alloy will have a different thermoelastic modulus from the low-distortion control.
The proposed effects should become significant at temperatures of at least 800 degrees Celsius under controlled strain rates.
The quantitative relationship between lattice-distortion magnitude and edge-versus-screw dislocation activity is not yet well defined.

contradictions.description: The formula TiZrHfNbMo0.1 is not near-equiatomic across all five elements: interpreted as stoichiometric coefficients, Ti, Zr, Hf, and Nb are each about 24.4 at.% while Mo is about 2.4 at.%.
The prediction requires only a different thermoelastic modulus, whereas the falsification rule requires thermoelastic property enhancement; a difference could occur without an enhancement.
